explanation: The V32I substitution increases hydrophobic bulk in the C-terminal dimer region, which despite not directly contacting indinavir, likely creates a subtle conformational strain through its proximity to the ligand binding site (8.2 Å minimum distance). This additional ~27 Å³ of van der Waals volume in a spatially constrained region probably distorts the local geometry of the protease dimer interface or active site architecture in a way that subtly misaligns indinavir's binding pose, reducing optimal intermolecular contacts without completely abolishing binding. The marginal effect size reflects that this is a peripheral perturbation—the mutation introduces steric crowding that destabilizes the inhibitor-bound conformation more than it stabilizes the apo enzyme.
